item.title: Further £10m Drugs Seizure Underlines Scale of Police Scotland Crackdown
item.description: A further £10m drugs seizure has added to one of Police Scotland’s largest crackdowns on organised crime, reinforcing efforts that are disrupting supply networks affecting communities across the Highlands and Scotland.The post Further £10m Drugs Seizure Underlines Scale of Police Scotland Crackdown appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Yellow Hoodies Launched to Champion Youth Volunteering and Mental Health
item.description: A new yellow hoodie has been launched through the High Life Highland Leadership Programme to recognise young people who volunteer in support of mental health charities, linking youth leadership with community wellbeing across the Highlands.The post Yellow Hoodies Launched to Champion Youth Volunteering and Mental Health appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: NFU Scotland Warns Dairy Farmers Face Crisis as Milk Prices Fall Below Costs
item.description: NFU Scotland has warned that dairy farmers are facing a deepening crisis as milk prices fall below production costs, urging urgent action from processors and the supply chain to protect rural jobs, food security and the future of Scottish farming.The post NFU Scotland Warns Dairy Farmers Face Crisis as Milk Prices Fall Below Costs appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Sutherland Set for £20m Pride in Place Investment Over Next Decade
item.description: Sutherland is set to receive up to £20m of long term Pride in Place funding over the next decade, giving local communities direct control over investment to support renewal, services and economic opportunity across the Highlands.The post Sutherland Set for £20m Pride in Place Investment Over Next Decade appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Westminster Refurb Bill Tops £20m Since Indy Referendum
item.description: Millions spent refurbishing Westminster buildings since 2014 has sparked criticism from SNP MPs, who say the figures highlight misplaced priorities at a time when Scottish families face rising costs and continued pressure on public services.The post Westminster Refurb Bill Tops £20m Since Indy Referendum appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: M&S Fragrance Sales Rise as Shoppers Seek Affordable Treats
item.description: Affordable fragrance is booming this Christmas, with Marks & Spencer reporting strong sales growth as shoppers turn to small, thoughtful treats, driving rising demand for its Discover range and limited-edition seasonal scents.The post M&S Fragrance Sales Rise as Shoppers Seek Affordable Treats appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: First Minister Chooses Highland Landscape for 2025 Christmas Card
item.description: A winter photograph of Loch Ossian taken by First Minister John Swinney has been chosen as his 2025 Christmas card, highlighting the importance of nature, wellbeing and connection during uncertain and challenging times.The post First Minister Chooses Highland Landscape for 2025 Christmas Card appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Suspected Avian Flu Cases Reported Among Geese at Highland Nature Reserve
item.description: Suspected avian flu cases have been reported among geese at a Highland nature reserve, prompting fresh guidance from RSPB Scotland as the risk to wild birds rises across the country this winter.The post Suspected Avian Flu Cases Reported Among Geese at Highland Nature Reserve appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Driving Home for Christmas – Travellers Urged to Plan Ahead as Festive Rush Begins
item.description: Festive travellers are being urged to plan ahead as Scotland’s roads and rail network prepare for the Christmas rush, with gritters ready, extra train services added and Police Scotland advising drivers to allow extra time and drive to conditions.The post Driving Home for Christmas – Travellers Urged to Plan Ahead as Festive Rush Begins appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Tesco Backs Ullapool Pupils With £1,500 Boost for Duke of Edinburgh Award
item.description: Young people in Ullapool are being given the chance to build confidence, skills and community spirit after a £1,500 Tesco grant helped safeguard the Duke of Edinburgh Award at Ullapool High School during a challenging time for rural education.The post Tesco Backs Ullapool Pupils With £1,500 Boost for Duke of Edinburgh Award appeared first on The Highland Times.
